findings.topic: orphan-sidecar sweep cannot see shared-cwd sub-agent spawns
findings.section: Phase 4 — tier (b) sweep catch-all / forward orphan-sidecar sweep
findings.criterion: 1 — Swarm spend visible going forward ("A new fleet run produces measured records for its sub-agent sessions")
findings.message: Steel-manning the premise: the plan's guarantee for the DOMINANT population (106 of 111 registry sessions are swarm) is "measured eagerly where wrapped, by sweep otherwise — never silently absent." The sweep's predicate is "sidecars whose dirname embeds a valid session marker but has no registry row." But a skill-layer sub-agent spawned WITHOUT the wrapper (the exact bypass tier (b) exists for) typically inherits the parent session's cwd — so its sidecar lands under the SAME munged project dirname as the parent. That dirname embeds the PARENT's session id, which DOES have a registry row, so the orphan predicate structurally never fires; the sub-agent's spend is either silently folded into (or mis-attributed against) the parent, or never minted at all. The "never invisible" claim is therefore false for precisely the population criterion 1 exists for, and the enforcement backstop (a grep conformance test over Anchor product code) cannot reach the actual spawner either — agy-dispatch is a skill in a different repo whose runtime `claude` invocations are model-driven prompts, not greppable Anchor call sites. The plan must either (a) require per-spawn distinct cwd/worktree so the dirname correlation holds per sub-agent, (b) correlate at sidecar-FILE granularity (per-file session UUID) rather than per-dir, or (c) honestly demote the tier-(b) guarantee from "never invisible" to "invisible unless wrapped" and make wrapper adoption a gating deliverable, not a named task.

findings.topic: CAS trust-model invariant contradicts its own writer table
findings.section: Phase 2 — CAS trust model, writers 2 and 5
findings.criterion: 3 — The latch cannot be burned hermetically
findings.message: Writer 5 declares the invariant "No measurement without a beacon, ever." Writer 2 (the backfill tool) holds no beacon — it runs precisely when the service is UNREACHABLE — yet mints `measured-backfill` records through "the identical claim path." Both statements cannot be true. As written, either the invariant is false (and the trust model's headline guarantee is rhetorical, not real), or backfill needs a beacon it structurally cannot have. The fix is a restatement, not a redesign — the true invariant is "no CAS consumption except by the current beacon holder OR the audited standalone operator CLI under its own admission predicate" — but a trust model whose single authoritative table contains a self-contradiction has not earned the word "authoritative," and the STUB-GATE tests pinning criterion 3 will pin whichever reading the implementer happens to choose.

findings.topic: two competing owners of deferred-retry measurement
findings.section: Phase 2 repair path / Phase 4 sweep scope / Phase 7 target set
findings.message: Phase 4 names the beaconed sweep "the single named owner of deferred retries," retrying every `finalize-deferred` record against the LIVE sidecar root on a ~30-minute cadence from the interim deploy checkpoint onward. Phase 2's repair path re-stamps the 3 poisoned records `finalize-deferred` and then asserts "the Phase 6 backfill measures them through the normal claim path." Both cannot own them: the sweep will reach those records phases earlier than backfill, reading the live root (which engine retention may have pruned differently than the Phase-0 snapshot), and whichever writer wins the exclusive-create claim forecloses the other. Consequences the plan does not resolve: (a) the repaired sessions may be stamped `measured` (sweep) rather than `measured-backfill` (backfill), so the Phase 7 outcome list's target set ("69 + 37 + 3 repaired-deferred") will not reconcile as written; (b) if the live sidecar was pruned but the snapshot copy survives, the sweep's retry fails first and the plan does not state whether a failed live retry leaves the record retryable for backfill or stamps a terminal-looking state. Name ONE owner per record class (e.g. sweep owns post-deploy deferrals; backfill exclusively owns pre-snapshot historical sessions, sweep skips them) or the "single named owner" claim is decorative.

The convention test "registering synthetic without the flag fails loudly" is unenforceable as specified: to detect that an unflagged registration is synthetic, the test must identify syntheticness by some signal other than the flag — which is name-sniffing, the exact mechanism the plan bans ("marker convention, never name-sniffing"). Either the test quietly reintroduces name-sniffing (acceptable ONLY inside the test as a tripwire, which the plan should say explicitly), or the guarantee degrades to "callers that remember the flag are excluded," which is a convention, not an enforcement — and per the project's own engine-vs-convention honesty table, it should be labeled as such. Also unstated: the migration step for EXISTING `__doctor__` registry rows that predate the flag; without it, criterion 2's "excluded from every surface" fails on day one for historical doctor sessions.

findings.topic: most-motivating deliverable sequenced last without a de-risking dry-run
findings.message: Steel-manning the ordering premise: "backfill LAST because the substrate must soak" was compelling when delay risked data loss — but Phase 0's plan-time frozen snapshot removes that risk entirely, and the claim path backfill reuses is soaked by every earlier phase regardless of when backfill's CORRELATION logic first runs. The intake motivation (106 unmeasured swarm sessions) is the single most user-visible deliverable, and it now lands in the second-to-last phase with zero earlier evidence that the correlation will actually recover a useful fraction. A read-only backfill DRY-RUN (correlate against the snapshot, print the recovered/no-sidecar/ambiguous-skipped outcome list, mint NOTHING) belongs in Phase 3 alongside the munging-function tests: it consumes no CAS, touches no record, and converts "we believe 55+ dirs correlate" from intake-time hope into measured plan-time fact — or reveals in week one that the recovery rate is poor while there is still budget to react.

Every heading carries two conflicting ordinals ("Phase 1 — Phase 0 — …", "Phase 2 — Phase 1 — …"), and the body text cross-references the INNER numbering ("Phase 6 backfill" meaning the heading labeled Phase 7). A Foreman wave parser or a human skimming headings will off-by-one these references. Collapse to one numbering scheme before handoff. (Out-of-scope per the inclusion test; noted at NIT only.)
